subject: public-health
intro: Public health leads to the population-scale side of health work — tracking disease, running prevention programmes, managing health services and shaping the policies behind them.

roles.title: Epidemiologists
roles.what: Investigate the determinants and distribution of disease, disability and other health outcomes in populations, and develop the means for their prevention and control.
roles.where: The Evidence-based Approaches to Public Health unit — epidemiological methods, biostatistics and interpreting the results of data analysis — is the working toolkit, applied to the morbidity and mortality trends the first unit teaches.

roles.title: Health Education Specialists
roles.what: Provide and manage health education programmes that help individuals, families and communities adopt and maintain healthy lifestyles, using data to plan, monitor and evaluate each programme.
roles.where: Planning and Management to Promote Health — assessing population needs, designing interventions and evaluating programmes — plus the communication unit's health literacy work are exactly what a health educator does.

roles.title: Community Health Workers
roles.what: Promote health within a community by helping individuals adopt healthy behaviours, advocating for residents' health needs and acting as liaison between communities and healthcare providers or agencies.
roles.where: The Factors Related to Human Health unit — social, cultural and economic determinants of health — explains the barriers workers navigate daily, and the policy unit's advocacy and coalitions strand is the outreach skill set.

roles.title: Medical and Health Services Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate medical and health services in hospitals, clinics, managed-care organisations and public health agencies, managing budgets, staffing and compliance.
roles.where: The Public Health and Health Care Systems unit — how those organisations are structured and function — and the budget and resource management topics of the planning unit are the management reality of the job.

roles.title: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists
roles.what: Review and analyse work environments and design programmes and procedures to control, eliminate and prevent disease or injury caused by chemical, physical and biological agents, inspecting workplaces and enforcing standards.
roles.where: The environmental factors strand of Factors Related to Human Health and the primary, secondary and tertiary prevention framework from the Profession and Science unit are the conceptual spine of workplace health protection.
